newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end touch lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end touch lower in thin trading.

text.p: Italian stocks closed slightly lower in thin trade on Monday with no real direction given London's holiday closure.

But investment bank Mediobanca and HPI industrial holding, two companies at the centre of a failed textiles mega merger, were major losers. Textile group Marzotto, however, the company which vetoed the deal at the weekend, held its own.
The All-share Mibtel index closed off 0.17 percent at 12,333 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended just 0.03 percent off at 18,393. Milan took little notice of Wall Street's performance.
The afternoon saw an acceleration of selling of HPI and Mediobanca, traders said, "probably by U.S. investors".
HPI closed 6.97 percent lower at 863.4 lire while Mediobanca ended 4.33 percent down at 10,166 lire. But Marzotto recovered from early losses to close 0.07 percent up at 12,417 lire.

In blue chips, which all saw thin volume, Olivetti performed well after the news of the acquittal of former chairman Carlo De Benedetti on alleged dividend stripping charges while he was head of the company several years ago. Olivetti closed 2.88 percent up at 499.9 lire.
Energy group ENI lost 0.54 percent to 8,648 lire and Fiat slipped 0.16 percent to 5,695.
Insurances staged a technical recovery with the exception of Fondiaria ahead of a board meeting.
IMI bank put on 1.68 percent to 14,769 lire, "probably gaining from a switch out of Mediobanca", one dealer said.
Total traded volume seen lower than Friday's at around 553 billion lire against Friday's 580 billion lire.
